Haegue Yang: She rebuilt one of Sol LeWitt's open-cube sculptures from Venetian blinds, turned it upside down and enlarged it 1,078 times.
Takashi Murakami: His new paintings trace how Edo-period ukiyo-e prints shaped Impressionism, down to a Monet with his own flowers in the clouds.
Seffa Klein: These are new works from her Fire Blankets series, made with molten bismuth.
Naoki Sutter-Shudo: He sands branches by hand until they read like relics.
Lub Poeem: Poeem turns found stones into vessels for flowers that wilt over the run of the show.
Calvin Miceli-Nelson: His paintings are dreamlike scenes where fragments of landscape drift.
Ramsés Noriega: La Raza Hoy is acrylic and marker on poster board, from 1968.
Luchita Hurtado: This painting is from her I Am series of the 1970s, looking down at her own body.
Takako Yamaguchi: This was her first solo museum show in Los Angeles: ten recent seascapes she calls abstractions in reverse.
Henri Matisse: La Gerbe is one of his final works and his only commission on the West Coast.
Olafur Eliasson: The show filled the Geffen with rings, mirrors and reflections that change as you walk through them.
